assumptions.statement: D7-v2 completes or closes candidate-local transitions; it does not derive the common K_4 to H_4 to h_4 structural crossing.

Candidate-local transition admission is evaluated on a fixed-topology, fixed-boundary, fixed-rank smooth stratum. Event and rank-change semantics remain explicit D8/D9 debt and do not narrow the eventual V4 target.
Candidate A may be reused only if its accepted D7 transition object is bound by canonical row hash without causal modification and its still-open global H_4 boundary remains explicit.
B requires an exact source-backed U_B. A writer copied from A, an EMA label, an untyped current outer product, or a post-hoc target chosen to retain B is not a derivation.
T_C is a derived decomposition P_M_Delta C and has no independent writer or resource authority; authoritative continuity writes C exactly once and T_C is then recomputed.

The initial C profile uses the D4-v2 lagged reference geometry and fixed selector during one candidate-local beat; D7G must reopen the earliest changed gate if global h_4 changes P_M_Delta, H_M, I_4M, R_C, or J_0.

Literal interventions are used only where ontologically lawful. Derived C-sector objects are controlled with on-manifold matched C states or algebraic probes rather than impossible independent T_C writes.

A terminal current-tranche closure localizes a missing theory or constitutive derivation. It is not candidate ranking, ontology rejection, or evidence that another candidate is more faithful to RC theory.
Analytical closure and finite-dimensional witnesses are design evidence, not runtime reachability, implementation evidence, temporal stability, or architecture selection.
Every D6-v2 current debt and every exact inherited debt remains accounted for by exact carry, explicit supersession, resolution, or terminal-candidate archival with a named reopening condition.
